newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila raises jail term for Britain convicted on drugs.
newsitem.headline: Manila raises jail term for Britain convicted on drugs.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Monday raised the jail sentence for a Briton convicted of heroin smuggling to 40 years from 35 and rebuked a British diplomat for what it said was an intrusion into the country's legal process.

The court said the trial judge misinterpreted provisions on scales of penalties by sentencing mobile phone salesman Nigel Richard Gatward in 1995 to 35 years imprisonment when a longer jail term should have been imposed.
The court also criticised a British consular officer for a letter it said he wrote to the court while it was reviewing the Gatward case.
The court, in a review released on Monday, also raised the jail term of Burmese seaman Aung Win, who had been originally convicted along with Gatward, to 40 years from 25 years.
Gatward had insisted during his trial that he was innocent. He appealed his conviction to the Supreme Court but later withdrew his appeal without giving a reason.
Aung Win did not join Gatward in his appeal to the Supreme Court.

The court said that after it rejected Gatward's motion to withdraw, the British consular officer wrote to the bench saying a convict who did not wish to continue with an appeal "would not need to prove merit but could simply notify the courts of his wish to withdraw and that would be the end of the matter".

The court said it was not the first time that members of foreign embassies and consulates "feel that they have a right to intrude into our judicial affairs and processes, to the extent of imposing their views on our judiciary, seemingly oblivious or arrogantly disdainful of the fact our courts are entitled to as much respect as those in their own countries."
It said it had written to the consul telling him "there is no arrangement whereby a foreign consular officer may intervene in a judicial proceeding in this court".
Gatward, 32, from Clapham in south London, was found guilty by a Manila judge of attempting to smuggle 5.2 kg (11.5 lb) of heroin out of the country in August 1994.
Philippine law prescribes the maximum penalty of death for people caught transporting or possessing heroin totalling 40 grams (1.4 ounces) or more.
